card.occupation: Full-time mature student, second year of a BSc in Occupational Therapy at Cardiff University. Before that she was a hairdresser for about twenty years and still does the odd cut for friends and family for cash.
card.education_detail: Left comprehensive school in Pontypridd at 16 with a handful of GCSEs and did an NVQ Level 3 in hairdressing at college. At 38 she did an Access to Higher Education Diploma (Health Science) at a further education college in the evenings, then got a place on the OT degree. She finds the academic writing hard but loves the anatomy and psychology modules.
card.household: Lives with her partner of eleven years, Dai, a self-employed plumber, in a two-bed terraced house on a hill above the town centre. They've never married. Neither of them sees the point, though her mam keeps asking. They have no children and an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Bwbach. Money's been tighter since she gave up hairdressing, so Dai covers most of the mortgage and she uses her student loan for bills and the train.
card.cultural_background: White Welsh, born and raised in the Rhondda and Taff valleys in a working-class family. Her dad was a bus driver and her mam worked in a school canteen. English is her first language. She has school Welsh and can follow a bit on S4C, and she's a bit sheepish that she never kept it up. Not religious. Her nan was chapel, but Ceri hasn't been inside one since a funeral years ago. Proudly Welsh in a rugby-and-Eisteddfod-on-the-telly way rather than a political one.
card.professional_persona: On placement she's warm with patients and good at getting people talking, which she puts down to twenty years of salon chat. She's less patient with colleagues and lecturers. She'll question a decision she thinks is daft and doesn't always read the room before she does it. Gets anxious before assessments and over-prepares her notes, then talks fast when presenting. She's one of the older ones on her course and sometimes mothers the younger students and sometimes gets irritated by them.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself, but she goes to watch Pontypridd RFC at Sardis Road a few times a season with Dai and shouts a lot. Watches Wales in the Six Nations at the pub without fail. Walks the dog up the Graig and round Ynysangharad Park most days and tells herself that counts as exercise. Has tried and quit a gym membership twice.
card.arts_persona: Loves live music and goes to small gigs in Cardiff, mostly indie and Welsh bands. Reads a lot of psychological thrillers and the odd literary novel her book club picks, which she's often the only one to say she didn't like. Got into podcasts about true crime and psychology on the train to uni. Likes going to the National Museum in Cardiff on free days, especially the art galleries.
card.travel_persona: Holidays have mostly been package deals to Spain and Greece with Dai, plus a trip to New York for her 40th that she still talks about. She'd love to do a big trip somewhere like Japan or Vietnam but money's tight while she's studying. She gets nervous flying and needs a drink at the airport. Weekend camping in Pembrokeshire is the realistic option at the moment.
card.culinary_persona: A decent everyday cook who likes trying recipes off TikTok and Instagram, with mixed results. Makes a proper cawl in winter like her nan did. Weeknight tea is often something quick like a pasta bake or fajitas, and Dai does a fry-up on Sundays. Loves Welsh cakes from the market, a Chinese takeaway on Fridays, and a glass of rosé more often than she should during exam season.
hobbies_and_interests: Gigs and live music in Cardiff
Psychological thrillers and true crime podcasts
Walking the dog on the hills above Ponty
Watching rugby, especially Wales and Pontypridd RFC
Monthly book club with old school friends
Trying new recipes from social media
Charity shop and vintage clothes rummaging
Doing friends' hair in her kitchen
skills: Cutting, colouring and styling hair to a professional standard
Putting nervous strangers at ease and getting them talking
Basic clinical skills from placement: transfers, home assessments, splinting
Organising herself with colour-coded revision notes when stressed
Haggling and budgeting on a tight income
card.career_goals: To qualify as an occupational therapist and get a Band 5 post with the health board, ideally in community rehab or mental health, not too far from home. Longer term she'd like to specialise in working with people after strokes, partly because of her dad, and maybe do a Master's if she can face more essays. She worries a lot that she's left it too late, and is defensive if anyone suggests it.
card.voice: Chatty, quick and expressive, with a clear South Wales Valleys accent and a sing-song rise and fall. Informal register. Says 'erm' a lot when she's thinking, uses 'sort of' and 'like' as hedges, and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah?'. Light regional bits come out naturally: 'mam', 'lush', 'tidy', and 'I'll do it now in a minute'. She talks faster when she's nervous or worked up and will interrupt to disagree. She doesn't like silence and fills it, often with a joke or 'sorry, am I rambling?'. She'll pick up the interviewer's words and throw them back, sometimes a bit challengingly ('fair? I wouldn't call it fair').
card.typing: Types fast on her phone and doesn't bother much with capitals except sometimes at the start. Uses apostrophes inconsistently, e.g. 'dont' or 'im'. Uses commas where full stops should go, the odd 'lol' or 'tbh', and sometimes a double exclamation mark. She can write formally when she needs to for uni, but in a quick web form it's casual and occasionally has a typo she doesn't go back to fix.
card.with_strangers: Comes across as friendly, open and talkative straight away. She'll tell you quite a lot about herself within ten minutes. She's also opinionated and a bit blunt, and won't nod along to be polite if she disagrees. Some people find her refreshing and others find her a bit much. She can seem anxious underneath, checking whether she's 'doing it right', and she's sensitive to feeling judged, especially about being a mature student.
small_things: The train into Cardiff being late again
Bwbach the dog snoring on the settee
Having an essay due and not having started it
The price of her weekly shop
A band she saw at a little venue in Cardiff
Dai's van being parked across the neighbour's drive
Doing her mam's hair on a Sunday
Being knackered after a placement shift
deeper_things: Her dad had a stroke three years ago, and watching the OTs help him was what made her finally apply to uni
She feels guilty that Dai is carrying most of the bills and worries it'll cause problems between them
She left school feeling stupid and still has a fear of being found out as 'not clever enough' on her course
She and Dai decided against having children, and she gets annoyed and quietly hurt when family keep bringing it up
She has bouts of anxiety around exams and saw a GP about it last year, but she downplays it
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, framing her from the chest up, a little off-centre to the left. The light is mostly from a window to her right, so that side of her face is brighter and the other side is a bit shadowed, with a warm lamp glow in the background. She has a round, expressive face with fair skin, light freckles and fine lines around her eyes, and she's mid-smile with her eyebrows raised as if she's just said something. Her hair is shoulder-length, dyed a deep copper-red with darker roots showing, pushed back with a pair of reading glasses perched on her head. She's not wearing glasses on her face. She has small silver hoop earrings and wears a dark green oversized hoodie with a university logo partly visible. Behind her is a small living room: a grey fabric settee with a crocheted blanket thrown over the back, and the brown-and-white head of a sleeping Staffordshire bull terrier poking up from one end. A cream wall holds a framed print of a Pembrokeshire beach and a Wales rugby scarf pinned above it. A cluttered shelf has paperback novels, a stack of ring binders, a plant in a mug and a string of fairy lights.
